<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917104_theRebbe_810" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917104_theRebbe_810__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Bittul (self-nullification) is necessary in all three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness, as it is the preparation for receiving Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the matter of bittul</t>
    <t s="1">(which is the preparation for the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="2">as mentioned above)</t>
    <t s="3">must be present in all three lines: Torah, service, and acts of kindness.</t>
    <t s="4">For Torah is a drawing down from above,</t>
    <t s="5">and the drawing down from above is specifically for one who is nullified,</t>
    <t s="6">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="7">"I dwell on high and holy, and with the crushed and lowly of spirit."</t>
    <t s="8">Therefore, the study of Torah must not be in a manner of a "yesh" (a self-aware entity) who studies; rather, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="9">"May my tongue answer Your word,"</t>
    <t s="10">like one who responds after the reader,</t>
    <t s="11">And similarly in the line of charity,</t>
    <t s="12">the matter of charity is</t>
    <t s="13">"to revive the spirit of the lowly."</t>
    <t s="14">And just as it is regarding charity in particular,</t>
    <t s="15">so too is it regarding all the mitzvos, which are called by the name "tzedakah" (charity),</t>
    <t s="16">that the fulfillment of mitzvos must specifically be with bittul,</t>
    <t s="17">that he fulfills the mitzvah of God</t>
    <t s="18">[and analogous to the bittul in the study of Torah,</t>
    <t s="19">where he feels that the Torah is "Your word"].</t>
    <t s="20">And similarly in the line of service, whose matter is</t>
    <t s="21">a level of bittul</t>
    <t s="22">(from below to above),</t>
    <t s="23">for this is that the service of prayer must specifically be with bittul, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="24">"A prayer of Dovid: Incline Your ear... and answer me, for I am poor and needy,"</t>
    <t s="25">and as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="26">"One does not stand to pray except from a state of heaviness of head," and Rashi explains: submission and lowliness.</t>
    <t s="27">And this is also what is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, in the maamar</t>
    <t s="28">(chapter 6)</t>
    <t s="29">regarding the matter of bittul in all three lines,</t>
    <t s="30">that regarding the study of Torah he brings what our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="31">"You will not find [Torah] in the haughty of spirit," etc.,</t>
    <t s="32">because the study of Torah must be with ultimate bittul,</t>
    <t s="33">like a student who receives from his teacher,</t>
    <t s="34">that at the time of the influence he must be nullified to the ultimate degree</t>
    <t s="35">("his lips drip myrrh"),</t>
    <t s="36">And similarly regarding prayer, he brings in the maamar the verse "A prayer of Dovid: Incline Your ear, God, and answer me, for I am poor and needy,"</t>
    <t s="37">that the request "Incline Your ear... and answer me" is because "I am poor and needy,"</t>
    <t s="38">And also the bittul that must be in the line of gemilus chasadim (acts of kindness) and all the mitzvos is hinted at there in the parable of the force of motion,</t>
    <t s="39">that in order to lift a heavy burden one must contract himself,</t>
    <t s="40">and in this is hinted the matter of bittul in the fulfillment of mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="41">For the mitzvos are clothed in physical things,</t>
    <t s="42">and the matter of clothing in physicality</t>
    <t s="43">(for a Jew)</t>
    <t s="44">is a difficult thing.</t>
    <t s="45">And this is what is hinted in the parable of the force of motion,</t>
    <t s="46">that just as in order to lift a heavy burden one must contract himself,</t>
    <t s="47">so too is it in the fulfillment of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="48">(which is analogous to a heavy burden)</t>
    <t s="49">that it must be with bittul.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The yud of the back of the dalet signifies ultimate bittul, which is a vessel to receive an incomparable influence, as explained through the parable of teacher and student.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">d)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, regarding the matter of the bittul of the letter yud</t>
    <t s="2">(which is at the back of the dalet)</t>
    <t s="3">it is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="4">and this is its language: The letter yud indicates bittul and self-diminution,</t>
    <t s="5">and this is Malchus of Atzilus, which has nothing of its own.</t>
    <t s="6">And it can be said that the intention in this is that it adds the matter of "having nothing of its own,"</t>
    <t s="7">for the matter of self-diminution,</t>
    <t s="8">even though it is a level of bittul,</t>
    <t s="9">nevertheless, some existence still remains</t>
    <t s="10">(and only that the existence is in a manner of diminution),</t>
    <t s="11">therefore it adds the matter of "having nothing of its own,"</t>
    <t s="12">which is</t>
    <t s="13">(as the language of the maamar there)</t>
    <t s="14">"in the ultimate bittul and lowliness."</t>
    <t s="15">And this will be understood based on what is explained by the Mitteler Rebbe in Biurei HaZohar</t>
    <t s="16">regarding the matter of "And also, indeed, she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother,"</t>
    <t s="17">that the level of bittul of an empty vessel comes specifically from the level of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="18">("my father")</t>
    <t s="19">specifically.</t>
    <t s="20">For from the contemplation of Binah</t>
    <t s="21">("my mother")</t>
    <t s="22">is produced an arousal in the manner of enthusiasm and commotion,</t>
    <t s="23">and the matter of the bittul of an empty vessel comes from the level of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="24">("my father")</t>
    <t s="25">specifically,</t>
    <t s="26">for the arousal of Chochmah is the matter of lowliness, to set oneself aside and nullify oneself completely.</t>
    <t s="27">And now it is understood,</t>
    <t s="28">that even the arousal in the manner of enthusiasm and commotion that comes from the contemplation of Binah,</t>
    <t s="29">since it too is "the daughter of my mother," a level of holiness,</t>
    <t s="30">it is in the category of bittul,</t>
    <t s="31">for "the entire matter of holiness is that it be in a state of ultimate bittul,"</t>
    <t s="32">and the difference between "the daughter of my mother" and "the daughter of my father" is only that the arousal born from Binah is not in a state of ultimate bittul.</t>
    <t s="33">For since Binah is understanding and comprehension,</t>
    <t s="34">a level of existence,</t>
    <t s="35">therefore the arousal born from it is in the manner of commotion.</t>
    <t s="36">In contrast, from the level of Chochmah one comes to ultimate bittul,</t>
    <t s="37">and this is that the bittul that comes through the contemplation of Binah</t>
    <t s="38">(which is a level of commotion and arousal)</t>
    <t s="39">is only in the category of externality,</t>
    <t s="40">in contrast to the bittul of Chochmah</t>
    <t s="41">(which is in silence)</t>
    <t s="42">which is a level of essential bittul, where he is nullified in his very essence.</t>
    <t s="43">And this is what is precisely stated in the maamar regarding the matter of "having nothing of its own,"</t>
    <t s="44">the level of ultimate bittul,</t>
    <t s="45">for since in bittul there are several levels as above,</t>
    <t s="46">therefore it specifies that the bittul</t>
    <t s="47">(of the letter dalet)</t>
    <t s="48">explained here is bittul in the ultimate sense</t>
    <t s="49">(which is a bittul even more elevated than the bittul of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="50">as will be explained later).</t>
    <t s="51">For specifically through such bittul does one become a vessel to receive an influence that is utterly incomparable to him,</t>
    <t s="52">as is explained in the parable of the teacher and student,</t>
    <t s="53">that through the student being in a state of complete nullification of existence,</t>
    <t s="54">in ultimate bittul and lowliness,</t>
    <t s="55">then specifically is he a vessel to receive the true influence of the teacher.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Tzemach Tzedek explains that receiving an incomparable influence requires the student to be an empty vessel, even nullifying prior attainments, analogous to the teacher's self-nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">e)</t>
    <t s="1">And the matter is as explained by the Tzemach Tzedek in Ohr HaTorah,</t>
    <t s="2">that the bittul of the student to receive the teacher's influence is analogous to the bittul of the teacher in order to influence the student,</t>
    <t s="3">for when the teacher imparts intellect to a student who is on his level,</t>
    <t s="4">although even then he must somewhat contract his intellect, nevertheless he does not need to set himself aside.</t>
    <t s="5">In contrast, when he wishes to impart intellect to a student who is not on his level at all, then he must set his very essence aside and contract his entire essence, etc.</t>
    <t s="6">And similarly regarding the bittul of the student,</t>
    <t s="7">that in order to receive an influence on his level</t>
    <t s="8">(even though even then he must be in a state of bittul,</t>
    <t s="9">nevertheless)</t>
    <t s="10">he does not need to be in ultimate bittul,</t>
    <t s="11">in contrast, in order to receive an influence that is not on his level at all,</t>
    <t s="12">just as the teacher who influences must set his essence aside as above,</t>
    <t s="13">so too is it regarding the student who receives</t>
    <t s="14">(as water reflects a face back to a face)</t>
    <t s="15">that he must be in a state of ultimate bittul.</t>
    <t s="16">And based on this he explains</t>
    <t s="17">(there)</t>
    <t s="18">what our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="19">"Rabbi Zeira fasted one hundred fasts so that the Babylonian Talmud would be forgotten from him," in order that he could receive the Jerusalem Talmud,</t>
    <t s="20">"that the intention,</t>
    <t s="21">that if he were not an empty vessel and had in his possession his prior attainments, he would not be able to receive the supernal influence of Eretz Yisrael."</t>
    <t s="22">And it can be said that the intention in this,</t>
    <t s="23">for on the surface it is not understood why Rabbi Zeira needed to fast one hundred fasts, etc.,</t>
    <t s="24">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="25">even before this he had the requisite bittul</t>
    <t s="26">[for from the very fact that he learned and attained the Babylonian Talmud, it is proven that he was in a state of bittul,</t>
    <t s="27">for the attainment of Torah is specifically through bittul, to the extent that any student whose lips do not drip myrrh, etc.],</t>
    <t s="28">and if so, why did he need to fast one hundred fasts, etc.,</t>
    <t s="29">and on this the Tzemach Tzedek explains,</t>
    <t s="30">that the intention in this is that he needed to be an empty vessel also from his prior attainments.</t>
    <t s="31">For since in order to receive a more elevated light one must be in a greater bittul,</t>
    <t s="32">therefore,</t>
    <t s="33">in order to be able to receive the supernal influence of Eretz Yisrael</t>
    <t s="34">[which is incomparably more elevated],</t>
    <t s="35">the bittul that he had previously was insufficient,</t>
    <t s="36">and he needed to fast one hundred fasts,</t>
    <t s="37">for fasts are a bittul of a person's existence,</t>
    <t s="38">and this bittul was still insufficient, and he also needed that "the Babylonian Talmud be forgotten from him"</t>
    <t s="39">(meaning that he needed not only a bittul of his existence in general, but also a bittul of his prior attainment),</t>
    <t s="40">and this is the true matter of an empty vessel,</t>
    <t s="41">which is empty also from the prior attainments.</t>
    <t s="42">And this is also the matter of "my sister, the daughter of my father,"</t>
    <t s="43">for the aforementioned level of an empty vessel is drawn specifically from the side of Chochmah and not from the level of Binah,</t>
    <t s="44">as explained in Ohr HaTorah there.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
